prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t name a single “best” roofer for Denver without knowing your exact neighborhood and needs, but I can help you find the best contractor and avoid common pitfalls. If you give me your ZIP code I can help narrow options or evaluate a short list you already have.

How to find the best roofer for hail damage in Denver
- Get multiple estimates (3 is a good target). Compare scope, materials, and written price breakdowns, not just total cost.
- Look for hail/insurance-claim experience. Roofers who regularly handle insurance claims understand Xactimate, policy language, and how to document hail damage so you get proper coverage.
- Check certifications from major shingle manufacturers (GAF Master Elite, Owens Corning Platinum Preferred, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster). These indicate training and better warranties.
- Ask about workmanship warranties (not just manufacturer) and what they cover and for how long.
- Confirm they are licensed/registered where required, bonded, and carry liability and workers’ comp insurance. Note: Colorado has no single statewide roofing license—cities/counties have requirements—so check with your city or county building department.
- Read recent local reviews (Google, Yelp) and check BBB ratings. Ask for recent Denver-area references and photos of completed hail repairs.
- Verify they will pull permits and arrange inspections if required by your locality.
- Prefer contractors who do a full roof inspection and provide photo documentation and a written scope (roofing, flashing, gutters, vents, decking condition).
- Beware of “storm chasers” who solicit door-to-door right after a storm, high-pressure sales tactics, or requests for full cash up front.

Important questions to ask any roofer
- How long have you been repairing hail-damaged roofs in Denver?
- Do you handle insurance claims? Can you help document damage and file an estimate?
- Which shingle brands and warranty levels do you install?
- Will you pull permits and handle inspections?
- Do you provide a written workmanship warranty? What does it cover and for how long?
- Can you provide local references and before/after photos of similar hail repairs?
- Are you insured (liability and workers’ comp)? Can you provide certificates?
- Do you use subcontractors? If so, who are they and how are they vetted?
- What is your payment schedule? Do you provide lien waivers?

Red flags
- Demands full payment up front or insists on cash-only.
- No physical address or local presence.
- No written contract or unwillingness to show references.
- They pressure you to sign immediately or claim the insurer will deny the claim unless you hire them.
- Extremely low bid compared with others (may cut corners).

Typical next steps for you
1. Get 3 written estimates with scope and materials.
2. Ask each to document damage with photos; request a sample insurance supplement if they handle claims.
3. Check references and online reviews.
4. Confirm permits, insurance, warranties, and payment terms in writing.
5. Don’t sign anything until you’ve compared all bids and confirmed the contractor’s credentials.

If you want, provide your ZIP code or a few roofer names you’re considering and I’ll help evaluate them or suggest top-rated local options and template questions/messages to send.
